text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Increased packet loss observed from CDN POP ap-southeast1 (SG) to customer edge nodes. Multiple healthchecks failing (backend 10.4.2.x). Auto-notify to #incidents.

maria: oncall here, I'm taking it. confirming impact?

alex: seeing p95 token latency jump from 120ms -> 800ms and ~30% packet loss on tcp from our egress. HTTP 502/504s up for a subset of customers in APAC.

maria: ok, scope -> is it only ap-southeast1 or cross-region?

alex: mostly ap-southeast1 POPs. ap-southeast2 looks fine. BGP updates looked normal, suspect last-mile ISP between our POP and the transit.

jin: dig and traceroute from an affected POP -> intermittent DNS timeouts too (resolves sometimes, NXDOMAIN other times). pasted output:```
traceroute to 203.0.113.21 (203.0.113.21), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.240.0.1  0.5 ms  0.3 ms  0.4 ms
 2  100.64.1.1  1.2 ms  1.1 ms  1.3 ms
 3  198.51.100.9  12.6 ms  *  11.9 ms
 4  *  *  *
 5  203.0.113.1  45.0 ms  44.9 ms  45.1 ms
```
shows * on hop 4 repeatedly, ~50% probe loss.

maria: that matches the packet loss windows. Could be upstream peering. Sylvain can you pull provider peering metrics?

sylvain: on it. checking transit provider telemetry and our POP router logs now. I've opened ticket with provider (TICKET-AP-8732). initial note: they're seeing partial packet drops on a transit interface.

ops-bot: runbook step triggered: 'edge-lastmile-packetloss' -> STEP 2: failover traffic to secondary POPs.

maria: do we want to shift traffic manually or let global loadbalancer failover? Risk of cache-regen costs.

alex: recommend gradual shift to ap-southeast2 and ap-east-1 to avoid cold cache stampede. I'll start a 10% route weight shift.

maria: go ahead. set healthcheck to 15s and lower DNS TTL to 30s for affected routing records.

jin: lowering TTL on cdn-*.redwood.ai zone now (ttl->30). propagation expected ~30s.

alex: issuing weight change:```
curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/routing/weights 
-H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED' 
-d '{"pop":"ap-southeast1","weights":{"ap-southeast1":0.9}}'
```
(gradual, watch metrics)

support-bot: Logged customer-facing incident banner draft: "Experiencing intermittent edge connectivity in APAC affecting latency and some requests. Engineers investigating."

maria: add note to put banner on status.redwood.ai once we confirm scope.

sylvain: provider confirmed a flappy interface and applied emergency mitigation (hardware level reroute). They report partial recovery ~+12m ago but see residual packet loss on path to 203.0.113.0/24.

alex: after shifting weights by 20%, error rates for affected customers dropped ~60%. p95 back to ~180ms. Still seeing occasional DNS lookup failures from some ISPs.

jin: interestingly, dig against 8.8.8.8 succeeds consistently, but our in-Pop resolvers hit timeouts ~20% of the time. Might be resolver chain hitting congested upstream recursors.

maria: plan: 1) keep gradual traffic shift to secondary POPs until provider confirms clean path 2) maintain customer banner 3) escalate resolver issues to infra networking 4) prepare for handoff in 30m if stable.

sylvain: opened concurrent ticket with DNS provider + included resolver traces. also requested BGP AS-path verification.

ops-bot: automation: spawned synthetic probe job from ap-se1 -> ap-se2 every 15s. results in the channel.

incident-bot: :hourglass_flowing_sand: Update: shift to 40% offload to other POPs in progress. Healthchecks improving.

alex: rolling config to reduce keepalive on POP frontends to mitigate half-open connections causing retries. command:```
kubectl patch deployment pop-frontend -n edge --type='json' -p='[ {"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/env/KEEPALIVE","value":"5s"} ]'```

Applied to 2/6 frontends so far.

jin: DNS provider replied: "we see spike in query latency from a subset of our recursors corresponding to AS-64501". They're validating with that provider.

maria: i'm going to call on-call phone rota to inform SRE manager and customers on PD list. alex, sylvain, keep logs of mitigation timings.

support-bot: Customer impact note saved to ticket INC-APAC-2026: "Intermittent CDN connectivity and DNS resolution failures in APAC (ap-southeast1), partial traffic offloaded to other POPs. Initial mitigation applied. Continued monitoring."

sylvain: provider confirmed full mitigation at 1888001460 (their time). they rerouted and cleared the flapping interface.

alex: we've seen error rates return to baseline in the last 3m. p95 ~140ms. DNS resolver errors reduced to <1%.

maria: good. I'll keep banner up for one hour then remove if stable. Preparing handoff to next oncall (sylvain will take network postmortem lead).

sylvain: I'll take handoff. action items during handoff: - coordinate with transit provider for postmortem - add extra synthetic probes from 3 regional recursors - validate resolver redundancy - update runbook with TTL change guidance.

maria: handoff notes: incident mitigated, provider reroute, traffic partially offloaded, keepmonitoring for 60m, next oncall sylvain. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: incident state -> MONITORING. severity: SEV2.

maria: closing primary coordination. tagging for postmortem and runbook updates. thanks team.

support-bot: Banner scheduled removal at +60m from now.

sylvain: (post-handoff) ticketing followup: will request complete BGP/PE logs from transit provider, and propose adding a play in runbook to preemptively shift weights when transit packet loss > 5% for 3 consecutive checks.

maria: ack. add retro items to INC-APAC-2026. we'll do a short postmortem tomorrow.
